subject: Incompletely crossed factors (grouping variables) and faceting

messages.author: cd8a02b90e537c02
messages.subject: Incompletely crossed factors (grouping variables) and faceting
parts:
Hello,

If I have a dataset with three factors that are incompletely crossed
(2 for faceting, one for grouping within a facet), along with a fourth
measurement variable, is it correct to say that it is not possible to
simplify each facet to remove the factor(s) that are not present? Here
is a toy example, where it makes sense that it would be difficult or
even unreasonable to remove the blank factor (shortmodel=="C" &
Auxiliary=="N")


var_level=c("L","L","L","L","L","L","L","L","M","M","M","M","M","M","M","M","H","H","H","H","H","H","H",
"H","L","L","L","L","M","M","M","M","H","H","H","H")
shortmodel=c("A","A","B","B","A","A","B","B","A","A","B","B","A","A","B","B","A","A","B","B","A","A","B","B","C","C","C","C","C","C","C","C","C","C","C","C")
Auxiliary=c("Y","Y","Y","Y","N","N","N","N","Y","Y","Y","Y","N","N","N","N","Y","Y","Y","Y","N","N","N","N","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y")
reltau=c(0.34,0.81,0.88,0.43,0.75,0.85,0.92,
0.19,0.72,0.75,0.11,0.44,0.23,0.57,0.98,
0.34,0.24,0.29,0.16,0.01,0.25,0.74,0.64,
0.14,0.91,0.03,0.68,0.89,0.86,0.90,0.73,
0.62,0.93,0.11,0.77,0.76)

tautest=data.frame(shortmodel,reltau,Auxiliary,var_level)
ggplot(tautest,aes(x=shortmodel,y=reltau)) + geom_boxplot() +
facet_grid(Auxiliary~var_level)

But if you look at it from this perspective, it might seem as though
it can be "easily" removed:

tautest=data.frame(shortmodel,reltau,Auxiliary,var_level)
ggplot(tautest,aes(x=shortmodel,y=reltau)) + geom_boxplot() +
facet_grid(Auxiliary~var_level) + coord_flip()

Thanks,

Chris

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Incompletely crossed factors (grouping variables) and faceting
parts:
On 12/13/2011 12:26 PM, Chris Gast wrote:
> Hello,
>
> If I have a dataset with three factors that are incompletely crossed
> (2 for faceting, one for grouping within a facet), along with a fourth
> measurement variable, is it correct to say that it is not possible to
> simplify each facet to remove the factor(s) that are not present? Here
> is a toy example, where it makes sense that it would be difficult or
> even unreasonable to remove the blank factor (shortmodel=="C"&
> Auxiliary=="N")
>
>
> var_level=c("L","L","L","L","L","L","L","L","M","M","M","M","M","M","M","M","H","H","H","H","H","H","H",
> "H","L","L","L","L","M","M","M","M","H","H","H","H")
> shortmodel=c("A","A","B","B","A","A","B","B","A","A","B","B","A","A","B","B","A","A","B","B","A","A","B","B","C","C","C","C","C","C","C","C","C","C","C","C")
> Auxiliary=c("Y","Y","Y","Y","N","N","N","N","Y","Y","Y","Y","N","N","N","N","Y","Y","Y","Y","N","N","N","N","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y","Y")
> reltau=c(0.34,0.81,0.88,0.43,0.75,0.85,0.92,
> 0.19,0.72,0.75,0.11,0.44,0.23,0.57,0.98,
> 0.34,0.24,0.29,0.16,0.01,0.25,0.74,0.64,
> 0.14,0.91,0.03,0.68,0.89,0.86,0.90,0.73,
> 0.62,0.93,0.11,0.77,0.76)
>
> tautest=data.frame(shortmodel,reltau,Auxiliary,var_level)
> ggplot(tautest,aes(x=shortmodel,y=reltau)) + geom_boxplot() +
> facet_grid(Auxiliary~var_level)

It can't be removed here because there is just a single, common
horizontal axis for each vertical facet, so within that they must have
the same set of x values.

> But if you look at it from this perspective, it might seem as though
> it can be "easily" removed:
>
> tautest=data.frame(shortmodel,reltau,Auxiliary,var_level)
> ggplot(tautest,aes(x=shortmodel,y=reltau)) + geom_boxplot() +
> facet_grid(Auxiliary~var_level) + coord_flip()

In this version, it can make sense to drop the missing factor.
Unfortunately, it is not "easy" because of how many things interact.
See a previous discussion about this:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/bb96b59a99c947b1/.
A "real" solution would be a horizontal box plot geom (which would mean
you don't need the coord_flip() which is what makes everything so hard),
but that does not exist. I tried to make one once, but wasn't successful.

> Thanks,
>
> Chris

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University
